top_opportunities: Stage1 gemm1 is the leader (31.60%, ~2x stage2). It now runs at 2 waves/SIMD (combined VGPR 240 = 112 arch + 128 accum; 32KB LDS/WG). The binding limiter for a 3rd wave is now LDS, not just VGPR: 32KB/WG pins it to 2 WG/CU (64KB/CU). To reach 3 waves/SIMD (33% occupancy) BOTH must drop: LDS to <=21KB/WG AND combined VGPR to <=170. VGPR trim alone no longer helps while LDS stays at 32KB.

Stage2 s2 (17.82%) sits exactly at combined VGPR 256 = the 2-wave boundary (512/256=2) with 28KB LDS. Cutting VGPR a little gains nothing; it needs <=170 combined VGPR AND <=21KB LDS together to unlock a 3rd wave. No scratch spill on either stage (good).

GPU fill is NOT the lever: gemm1 launches 69632 CTAs and s2 8704 CTAs vs 304 CU (massively oversubscribed). This is pure per-wave occupancy / MFMA-issue latency hiding (latency sub-case C2: too few resident waves), not a grid/split-K problem.

Consider fusing stage1->stage2 to avoid the a2 (fp8 intermediate) + a2s round-trip through HBM between the two kernels; stage1 already fuses SiLU and the intermediate fp8 block-scale quant, so the remaining inter-stage cost is the a2/a2s materialization. Secondary vs the occupancy lever.
